blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A batch worker creates `batch.lock` when a job starts and deletes it in the `finally` around the job. On deploy the orchestrator sends SIGTERM to the JVM, waits 30 seconds, then starts the new version; the service registers no shutdown hook of its own. A job that takes ten minutes was running. The new version refuses to start because `batch.lock` still exists. Why?

options.text: It never ran, since the JVM ran its shutdown sequence and then halted the worker thread where it was
options.says: SIGTERM starts the shutdown sequence: hooks run, then the JVM halts, and threads still in try never run their finally

options.text: It never ran, since SIGTERM skips the shutdown sequence and halts the worker thread where it was, as SIGKILL does
options.says: SIGTERM does run the shutdown sequence (the shutdown hook ran on SIGTERM); only SIGKILL and halt skip it

options.text: It ran once SIGTERM interrupted the worker thread, but the job still held the file open, so the delete failed
options.says: the shutdown sequence doesn't interrupt application threads; the JVM halts them where they are, so finally never ran

options.text: It ran once SIGTERM interrupted the worker thread, but the new version started before the delete reached the disk
options.says: the shutdown sequence doesn't interrupt application threads, so the finally never ran at all

origin.section: finally Runs Only When the Thread Leaves try: exit, halt and a Killed JVM Skip It

questions.stem: A rate limiter has `int takeAll() { try { return tokens; } finally { tokens = 0; } }`, where `tokens` is an `int` field. With `tokens` at 7, a caller runs `int got = limiter.takeAll();`. What are `got` and `tokens` afterwards?

options.text: `got` is 7 and `tokens` is 0, since the `return` read the field before the reset ran
options.says: the return evaluated tokens, 7, before finally ran; the reset changed the field, not the value already being returned

options.text: `got` is 0 and `tokens` is 0, since the reset ran before the `return` read the field
options.says: finally does run before the method returns, but the return's value was evaluated first

options.text: `got` is 7 and `tokens` is 7, since the `return` left the method before the reset could run
options.says: finally runs on every way out of try, return included

options.text: `got` is 0 and `tokens` is 7, since the `return` passed the field by reference and the reset changed it
options.says: an int is returned as a value, not a reference; only a mutable object returned by reference can be changed by finally

origin.section: A return Fixes Its Value Before finally Runs, but the Object Can Still Change

questions.stem: A DAO method runs a query; its `catch (SQLException e)` throws `new DataAccessException("load failed", e)`, and its `finally` calls `conn.close()`. One night the query fails with a deadlock and `conn.close()` then throws `SQLException: connection reset`. What does the caller's log show?

options.text: The reset, with no cause and nothing suppressed, since the `finally`'s exception replaced the one in flight
options.says: an exception thrown from finally replaces the one in flight; nothing attaches the earlier ones to it

options.text: The reset, with the `DataAccessException` as its cause, since the JVM links the `finally`'s exception to the one in flight
options.says: nothing links them: the caller sees C with no cause and no suppressed exception

options.text: The `DataAccessException`, with the deadlock as its cause, since an exception from `catch` wins over one from `finally`
options.says: the finally's own throw ends it and replaces whatever was in flight, including one thrown from catch

options.text: The `DataAccessException`, with the reset suppressed on it, since the JVM records the `finally`'s exception on the one in flight
options.says: only code that calls addSuppressed, such as the nested cleanup or try-with-resources, records a suppressed exception; a plain finally doesn't

origin.section: An Exception From finally Replaces the One in Flight and Skips the Cleanup After It

questions.stem: A command-line tool starts a daemon thread that uploads a report and deletes the local temp copy in its `finally`. `main` prints `done` and returns while the upload is still in progress, and nothing else runs. What happens to the temp copy?

options.text: It stays on disk, since the JVM exits once `main` returns and halts the daemon thread where it is
options.says: with no non-daemon thread left the JVM shuts down and halts the daemon thread where it is; its finally doesn't run

options.text: It stays on disk, since a daemon thread skips its `finally` even when its `try` ends normally
options.says: a daemon thread runs finally like any thread when it leaves try; it is skipped only because the JVM ends first

options.text: It is deleted, since the JVM waits for the daemon thread's `finally` before it exits
options.says: the JVM doesn't wait for daemon threads; it halts them, and finally clauses are not executed

options.text: It is deleted, since the JVM interrupts the daemon thread at exit, which unwinds it through its `finally`
options.says: the JVM doesn't interrupt daemon threads at exit; it halts them where they are

origin.section: finally Runs Only When the Thread Leaves try: exit, halt and a Killed JVM Skip It

concepts: finally runs only when the thread leaves try: System.exit, SIGTERM, Runtime.halt, SIGKILL and JVM exit while a daemon thread is in try all skip it, while an interrupt does not.
The value a return statement returns is evaluated before finally runs, so changing a primitive field or variable in finally doesn't change the result.
